To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a simple approach to predict the oxygen diffusion of concrete is established.
the oxygen diffusivities of (non) carbonated cementitious material can be expressed by a multi-factor model.
a comprehensive approach to calculate the diffusivity of oxygen of (non) carbonated cementitious material is developed.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: (1) to establish a comprehensive approach to calculate the diffusivity of noncarbonated cementitious material, (2) to develop a comprehensive approach to predict the oxygen diffusivities of carbonated cementitious material and to investigate the effects of carbonation on the oxygen diffusive properties of cementitious material.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the oxygen diffusivities of non-carbonated cementitious materials could be expressed as the function of the diffusivity of oxygen in air, the tortuosity, the porosity of hardened cement paste and the volumetric fraction of aggregates, while that of carbonated cementitious material could be expressed as a function of those factors mentioned above plus the carbonation depth.
the oxygen diffusivities of noncarbonated and carbonated concrete can be calculated by the following equations, respectively.

the oxygen diffusivities of noncarbonated cement paste and mortar are expressed by a multi-factor equation and the oxygen diffusivites of carbonated cement paste and carbonated mortar are expressed by the oxygen diffusity of the noncarbonated cementitious material divided by the porosity of the noncarbonatied cementitious material divided with the porosity of carbonated cementitious material.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oxygen diffusivities of non-carbonated cementitious materials could be calculated by the diffusivity of air and tortuosity, and that the oxygen diffusing through carbonated concrete is mainly due to the diffusion through carbonation products, and the oxygen diffusing in air is not important for the oxygen diffusing to carbonated concrete.

the diffusivity of oxygen in cementitious materials is mainly determined by the tortuosity and porosity of cementitious materials and the oxygen diffusivities in cementitious materials are in the range of 1.2-3.5×10 ^{-11} m ^{2} s ^{-1}.
the oxygen diffusivities of cementitious materials can be calculated by a function of porosity, tortuosity and volumetric fraction of air voids in concrete.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the oxygen diffusivities of non-carbonated cementitious materials are mainly determined by the diffusivity of air and tortuosity, and the oxygen diffusities of carbonated materials are determined by the reduced porosity due carbonation and the tortuosity.
a comprehensive approach to calculate the diffusivity of oxygen in concrete can be established, which can be easily applied to the service life determination and the durability designing of concrete.
the oxygen diffusivities of cementitious materials can be predicted by a simple approach, which can be easily used in engineering practice.
